title: SlideSparse: Fast and Flexible (2N-2):2N Structured Sparsity
claim: A cheap transformation lets milder sparsity patterns use existing sparse hardware, with measured speedups approaching the theoretical limit.
layout: 2 panels: left vertical flow of matrices, right line plot with theoretical curve
description: Two panels. Panel (a), on the left, shows a vertical pipeline. A purple grid labeled '6:8 Sparsity Matrix' (two rows, eight columns, some cells white) feeds into a green downward arrow labeled 'SlideSparse'. That produces a wider 12-column grid with a different pattern of white cells. A second green arrow labeled 'cuSPARSELt' leads to a compact 6-column purple 'Compressed Matrix' with a small blue striped block labeled '2 bit indices'. Panel (b), on the right, sits in a rounded light-gray box. It is a line plot of speedup over cuBLASLt (y-axis, 1.0 to 2.0) against sparsity (x-axis: 2:4, 4:6, 6:8, 8:10). A dotted gray theoretical curve decays from 2.0 down toward about 1.25. Three colored lines with markers (Qwen2.5-14B in blue circles, Qwen2.5-7B in orange diamonds, Llama3.2-3B in green triangles) track just below that curve. The eye goes first to the purple matrices, then to the curves hugging the theoretical limit.
caption: \textbf{SlideSparse extends 2:4 Sparse Tensor Cores to the $\mathbf{(2N{-}2):2N}$ sparsity family.} (a) SlideSparse transforms 6:8 weights into 2:4-compliant blocks, enabling sparsity acceleration. (b) End-to-end speedup on A100 (INT8, seq\_len$=$8K) approaches the theoretical limit $S_{\max}=N/(N{-}1)=3/2, 4/3, 5/4, ...$ (\S[ref]).
abstract: NVIDIA's 2:4 Sparse Tensor Cores deliver 2x throughput but demand strict 50% pruning -- a ratio that collapses LLM reasoning accuracy (Qwen3: 54% to 15%). Milder $(2N-2):2N$ patterns (e.g., 6:8, 25% pruning) preserve accuracy yet receive no hardware support, falling back to dense execution without any benefit from sparsity. We present SlideSparse, the first system to unlock Sparse Tensor Core acceleration for the $(2N-2):2N$ model family on commodity GPUs. Our Sliding Window Decomposition reconstructs any $(2N-2):2N$ weight block into $N-1$ overlapping 2:4-compliant windows without any accuracy loss; Activation Lifting fuses the corresponding activation rearrangement into per-token quantization at near-zero cost. Integrated into vLLM, SlideSparse is evaluated across various GPUs (A100, H100, B200, RTX 4090, RTX 5080, DGX-spark), precisions (FP4, INT8, FP8, BF16, FP16), and model families (Llama, Qwen, BitNet). On compute-bound workloads, the measured speedup ratio (1.33x) approaches the theoretical upper-bound $N/(N-1)=4/3$ at 6:8 weight sparsity in Qwen2.5-7B, establishing $(2N-2):2N$ as a practical path to accuracy-preserving LLM acceleration. Code available at https://github.com/bcacdwk/vllmbench.
